title: First-record ceiling for byte-limited profiling
lead: With a byte limit, squalify reads a first record that is longer than the limit to its end, however long (sq-35, owner decision 2026-10-28: "No ceiling, document it"). Add an opt-in ceiling, `ProfileOptions.MaxFirstRecordBytes` and `--max-first-record-bytes N`: when the first record, line terminator included, is longer than N, squalify stops reading at N+1 bytes instead of reading on. **Not in this slice:** a ceiling on any record after the first; a default ceiling (off by default, so today's behavior and descriptors are unchanged); sampling from the middle or end of a file.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A consumer that knows its format has short header lines (a sweep-table splitter that classifies a file from its first 1 MiB) wants to refuse a huge file with no line breaks without reading all of it. Today `ScopeCut.FindLineCut` keeps reading in 4 KiB chunks until it finds a terminator or the end of the file, so a multi-gigabyte file with no line breaks is read whole. Follows sq-35, which chose "read it whole, no ceiling" as the default and said the overshoot is documented, not capped; this adds the opt-in without reopening that decision.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `ProfileOptions` and `ProfileOptions.Create` (`src/squalify/Descriptor/Options.cs`), `ScopeCut` (`src/squalify/Sources/ScopeCut.cs`), `Profiler` (validation), the CLI option in `src/squalify.Cli/CommandFactory.cs`
- descriptor.md and `src/squalify/Json/DescriptorWriter.cs` only if the answer to Q1 adds a scope member or an issue code
- design.md (the "Byte limit" paragraph), user-guide.md ("Reading only a prefix" and the CLI usage block), README; how-it-works.md if the pipeline text changes

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- **Off by default:** a file whose first line is longer than `--max-bytes`, profiled without a ceiling, gives the same descriptor as before (golden, `scope.bytesRead` is the whole first line).
- **Boundary:** a first record of exactly N bytes (terminator included) is accepted; N+1 bytes triggers the ceiling.
- **Reads at most N+1 bytes:** a counting `IProfileSource` over a large file with no line break, with `MaxFirstRecordBytes` N, shows that no more than N+1 bytes were read in total, including when `MaxBytes` is larger than N+1 (the ceiling check runs before the sniff of the window, so the window read does not pass N+1).
- **Only the first record:** a later record longer than N does not trigger it; a first record that ends inside N does not, even when the second record is longer than N.
- **Validation:** N of zero or less raises `SqualifyException`, like `MaxBytes`; the CLI parses `--max-first-record-bytes` and rejects a non-positive or non-numeric value.
- **Failure shape (pending Q1):** the chosen outcome is pinned: the exception text, or the issue code and what scope and the profile hold (`bytesRead` is at most N+1).
- **Without a byte limit (pending Q2):** pin whichever answer is chosen: either the ceiling applies and a long first line fails, or the option is rejected without `--max-bytes`.
- **Cuts (pending Q3):** each of these is pinned to the chosen rule: a bare CR as the N-th byte (is the record N or N+1 once the LF after it is read?); a CRLF whose LF is byte N+1; UTF-16LE, UTF-16BE and UTF-32 first lines of N and N+2 or N+4 bytes (N not a multiple of the unit width); a binary file with no CR or LF (not a text record, so presumably unaffected).
- Mutation-check: changing `>` to `>=` at the boundary and dropping the early stop each fail a test above.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Build, test and format pass; `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: The owner commits. Do not commit; never add Co-Authored-By or similar lines.
